thread:
emily_support: Customer reports p99 latency for text-generation API jumped to ~1.5-1.8s since ~03:30 UTC. Multiple tenants affected, support tickets opened. Any infra changes around 03:20-03:35?

alice_oncall: seeing it in dashboards too — p95 ~240ms, p99 ~1.7s across several hosts in us-west-2. No app deploys in that window.

ben_infra: we rolled CUDA/driver update to gpu-pool-3 at 03:18 as part of scheduled security patch (CUDA 12.2.1, driver 535.x). Rollout was limited to pool-3 (10 hosts) and then continued to autoscale yesterday night.

carla_runtime: can you DM a sample trace id? I want the model call and to look at kernel timing and kv cache hits.

emily_support: trace id from customer: trace-0a9f3e. Repro: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"model":"gpt-large","prompt":"lorem ipsum"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate — they hit it repeatedly and p99 is high.

frank_cs: three paying customers opened escalation calls. One reported timeouts from their end (2s) and automatic retries causing duplicate tokens billed. They want ETA/mitigation.

dan_sre: I'm pulling host metrics now. Early signs: on hosts with driver update, GPU kernel time per token has ~30-40% spikes and NVMe latency shows tail latency spikes. Also seeing NVMe resets in dmesg on two hosts.

infra-bot: deployment:cuda-driver-535 rolled to gpu-pool-3 at 2026-03-17T03:18:12Z by ben_infra.

ben_infra: hmm NVMe resets — those hosts share a new kernel module version we landed with the driver's packaging. I'll run iostat and nvme-cli diagnostics.

carla_runtime: from trace-0a9f3e: KV cache miss rate jumped from 4% -> 22% and full-token generation times include long pauses between kernel launches. Could be driver/kernel interaction causing scheduling delays.

alice_oncall: mitigation plan proposal: 1) stop new traffic to gpu-pool-3 (drain), 2) roll back driver on pool-3 to previous known-good (CUDA 12.1 + driver 525.x), 3) route traffic to gpu-pool-2 temporarily. Anyone oppose?

ben_infra: starting rollback on pool-3 (hosts g3-01,g3-02 first). Using automation:
```
ansible-playbook -i inventories/gpu-pool-3 rollback-driver.yml --extra-vars "driver_version=525.89"
```
Should be quick but will require node reboots. I'll cordon/drain before reboot.

dan_sre: parallel steps: increase NVMe queue depth on affected hosts to try to reduce tail latency (temporary), and disable the new kernel module if possible. I'll coordinate with ben.

alice_oncall: also enabling a traffic-split rule to divert 40% of prod traffic away from pool-3 to pool-2 to reduce load while rollbacks proceed.

emily_support: told customers: "We’re seeing a platform-wide p99 increase affecting some regions. We’re draining a subset of GPUs and reverting a recent driver update; will update in 20m." They replied :thumbsup: but want confirmation when p99 drops.

ben_infra: rollback started 03:42 on g3-01 and 03:45 on g3-02. Rebooting now.

carla_runtime: watching traces — after g3-01 reboot and rollback, I see sample traces from that host show p99 down to ~300ms for that host's traffic. Good sign.

dan_sre: NVMe tail drops after reboot/rollback on g3-01. iostat snapshot before/after:
```
# before (affected)
Device:  rrqm/s wrqm/s r/s w/s  rkB/s wkB/s  avgrq-sz  avgqu-sz  await r_await w_await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1   0.00   0.00 200.0 100.0  8000  3200   20.0     12.5     4.5   0.9     5.1   0.25   50.0
# avgqu-sz high, tail very spiky
\n# after rollback
nvme0n1   0.00   0.00 180.0  80.0  7200  2800   20.0      1.2     1.8   0.6     2.0   0.10   18.0
```

ben_infra: rolling the rest of pool-3 now. ETA 20m to finish. I'll keep them cordoned until each host confirms nvme/kern logs are clean.

frank_cs: relaying update to customers. They asked whether we’ll adjust billing for duplicate tokens from retries — billing/finance will handle credits if customers request.

alice_oncall: after ~12 minutes into rollback, cluster-wide p99 across prod is back down to ~320ms and p95 ~210ms. Monitoring closely for any rebound.

carla_runtime: will open a runbook PR to detect this class of regression automatically: correlate driver/kernel changes with KV cache miss rate and nvme tail latency and trigger rollback if p99 increases >20% for 10m.

dan_sre: creating incident ticket INC-2026-0317-47 with notes and timeline. Postmortem requested — include driver package details, package pipeline checks, and e2e perf smoke test before rollout.

ben_infra: root cause hypothesis: driver packaging shipped an incompatible kernel module variant that interacts poorly with our NVMe qdisc under high concurrency, producing NVMe resets and GPU kernel stalls. We'll reproduce in staging with stress tests (nvme stress + perf firing) before re-rolling.

alice_oncall: good triage. For now: rollback complete on pool-3, all nodes back to 525.x, traffic un-muted. Please keep an eye for any slow tails for the next 2 hours.

emily_support: customers confirmed latency is back to normal. Closing escalation but keeping tickets open until postmortem done. :white_check_mark:

frank_cs: thx all — will coordinate customer follow-ups and credits if needed.

carla_runtime: follow-up action items: 1) reproduce in staging, 2) add pre-rollout perf smoke gates, 3) add nvme/reset alert correlate with p99.

dan_sre: assigning owners in incident ticket. Will schedule a postmortem meeting tomorrow.

alice_oncall: incident closed for now — re-open if we see p99>1s again. :rotating_light:
